title: Practice: Atomic Number and Mass Number

questions.stem: An atom is represented as ²⁷₁₃Al. How many neutrons does this atom contain?
questions.explanation: In atomic notation, the mass number (27) is on top and the atomic number (13) is on the bottom. Neutrons = Mass number - Atomic number = 27 - 13 = 14. A common mistake is to think the mass number directly gives the number of neutrons, but it actually counts protons + neutrons together.

questions.stem: Two atoms are represented as ³⁵₁₇Cl and ³⁷₁₇Cl. What is the same about these two atoms?

options.text: They have the same number of neutrons
They have the same mass number
They have the same number of protons
They have the same total number of subatomic particles

questions.explanation: Both atoms have an atomic number of 17, meaning they both contain 17 protons. This is why they are both chlorine atoms - the atomic number (number of protons) defines the element. They have different mass numbers (35 and 37) and therefore different numbers of neutrons (18 and 20 respectively). These are isotopes of chlorine.

questions.stem: A potassium atom has 19 protons and 20 neutrons. What is its atomic notation?
questions.explanation: The mass number = protons + neutrons = 19 + 20 = 39. In atomic notation, mass number goes on top and atomic number (protons) goes on the bottom: ³⁹₁₉K. A common mistake is to put the atomic number on top, or to use the neutron number instead of calculating the mass number.

questions.stem: Why is the atomic number always smaller than or equal to the mass number?

options.text: Because atoms always have more electrons than protons
Because the mass number includes both protons and neutrons, while the atomic number counts only protons
Because the mass number counts electrons as well
Because heavier elements always have more neutrons than lighter ones

questions.explanation: The atomic number counts only protons, while the mass number counts protons plus neutrons. Since atoms have zero or more neutrons, the mass number is always greater than or equal to the atomic number. The only exception is hydrogen-1, which has no neutrons and where A = Z = 1.

questions.stem: An unknown atom has a mass number of 40 and contains 21 neutrons. Which element is it?
questions.explanation: Atomic number = Mass number - Neutrons = 40 - 21 = 19 protons. The element with atomic number 19 is potassium (K). A common error is to assume the number of neutrons equals the atomic number, or to look up the element using the mass number instead of the calculated atomic number.
